plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Direction/magnitude of gain and lag/time-to-settle, which set controller sign, feedforward level for 0.5, and required integral/settling time.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater hypothesis is right, y will rise from ~0.231 with short lag (tens of s) toward ~0.35-0.50, with positive early slope flattening over 300 s; slope at end indicates how close to equilibrium.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Tests H4/H2: whether output decays at u=0, how fast, and to what ambient level, which sets controller need for steady heating and integral time; long 480 s hold also separates noise from trend.
experiments.expected_observation: If heat-loss hypothesis is right, y will decay from ~0.47 toward ~0.10-0.20 over 480 s with curved exponential shape, ~50% of drop in first ~100-150 s, plus +/-0.02 sensor scatter; flat hold or rise would falsify H4.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Tests H5/H6 linearity and steady-state gain: a second amplitude 0.4 vs 0.3 separates linear from saturating response and estimates input needed to hold 0.5, which sets feedforward and integral authority for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain first-order hypothesis is right, y will rise from ~0.12 with short lag toward ~0.6-0.7 equilibrium, reaching ~0.5-0.6 after 280 s with flattening but still positive end slope; +/-0.03 scatter. Flat or falling trace would falsify H1/H5.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Narrows steady-state input for y=0.5 and tests linearity/symmetry by approaching target from above; distinguishes whether u~0.33 holds 0.5 versus needing <=0.30 or >=0.38, which sets controller feedforward and integral authority.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain first-order hypothesis is right, y will decay from ~0.54 toward ~0.48-0.52 over 140 s with curved flattening and end slope near zero, plus +/-0.025 scatter; continued rise above 0.56 would falsify estimated gain/H6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Narrows steady-state input for y=0.5 by approaching from above at 0.27; separates u*~0.275 holding band versus needing <=0.25 or >=0.30, which sets controller feedforward and integral authority.
experiments.expected_observation: If linear first-order heater with ambient ~0.15 and K~1.28 is right, y will decay from ~0.557 toward ~0.49-0.51 over 175 s with curved flattening, reaching ~0.51-0.53 with still slightly negative end slope, plus +/-0.03 scatter/outliers; continued flat at ~0.57 or rise would falsify estimated u*~0.275 and H5/H6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Narrows steady-state input for y=0.5 to within ~0.01 by approaching from above at 0.25, which sets controller feedforward and integral authority to stay in 0.475-0.525 band.
experiments.expected_observation: If linear first-order heater with ambient~0.15, K~1.3, tau~150s is right, y will decay from ~0.526 toward ~0.48-0.51 equilibrium, reaching ~0.50-0.52 after 200s with flattening slope near zero, plus +/-0.03 scatter/outliers; flat hold at ~0.53 or continued rise would falsify estimated u*~0.26 and H5/H6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Narrows steady-state input for y=0.5 to within ~0.01 by testing 0.26 from just below band, separating u*~0.26 holding band versus needing <=0.25 or >=0.27, which sets controller feedforward and integral authority.
experiments.expected_observation: If linear first-order heater with ambient~0.15, K~1.35, tau~150s is right, y will rise slowly from ~0.477 toward ~0.50-0.51 equilibrium, reaching ~0.49-0.51 after 200s with flattening slope near zero, plus +/-0.03 scatter; flat hold far below 0.48 or rise above 0.55 would falsify estimated u*~0.26.

ledger.statement: Steady-state y is monotonically increasing in u: u=0.3 rises to ~0.47 still rising, u=0.4 rises to ~0.54 still rising, u=0.33 holds ~0.571, u=0.27 holds ~0.527, u=0.26 holds ~0.483 in-band flat, u=0.25 decays to ~0.47-0.49 borderline-low.

Response has lag/inertia with 63% time ~120-180s: E2 decays ~63% in ~176s, E1/E3 still rising after 280-300s with slopes 0.0005/0.0012, small steps E4/E5/E6 settle within ~140-200s with end slopes 0.0004/0.0002/-0.0002, E7 flat 200s at 0.26 with slope -0.0.
No large dead zone at operating levels: u=0.25, 0.26, 0.27, 0.3, 0.33 and 0.4 all produce measurable heating/holding >0.4 versus ambient, with ordered steady levels.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward room level ~0.10-0.20 due to heat loss, reaching ~0.15 mean after 480s with zero end slope, rather than holding.

Static gain is approximately linear with (y_ss-ambient)/u ~1.27-1.40: ambient ~0.15 predicts ~0.49 at 0.25 observed ~0.47-0.49, ~0.49-0.50 at 0.26 observed 0.483, ~0.53 at 0.27 observed 0.527, ~0.57 at 0.33 observed 0.571, ~0.55 at 0.3 and ~0.69 at 0.4 not yet reached.

Steady-state input to hold target y=0.5 is ~0.26-0.27 centered ~0.265, because u=0.33 holds 0.571 above, u=0.27 holds 0.527 just above band, u=0.26 holds 0.483 low-in-band flat, u=0.25 holds 0.466-0.49 just below band.

Sensor noise/outliers are substantial ~0.02-0.05 requiring averaging/filtering: E2/E3/E5/E6 show +/-0.03 scatter and 0.04-0.08 dips including E6 end cluster to 0.438, E7 shows tighter +/-0.01 core plus isolated 0.04 dips, so only trends >0.05 over 100s are reliable dynamics.
